output.name: Kavet — The Drop Spindle
output.myth: Mother Hesk sat at the pole with her spindle, drawing the string out thin and winding it on the whorl so the islands would not drift. Then Aun came up the north cliffs with his knife, wanting to know how far the wind went. He cut. The string went slack in her hand, but the spindle kept turning, because a whorl does not know it has been cut. The yarn it still held ran off up and to the left, toward the Knife-Beak, where the shore birds were left with nothing to wind. The Gulls, watching from above the Lidded Jar, say the loose end is still in Hesk's fist and she is counting the turns. Out in the west hangs the Single Mitten, the red one Tavo tore off the line of the girl Mesk, and Hesk has not asked for it back. When your own thread snags on the rocks, do not curse it. Hesk spins it still, and her count is patient. Keep your hands busy. A spindle that stops is a spindle that falls.
output.finding: Find the Single Mitten in the west, then go one hand-span (about 20°) east of it to reach the Drop Spindle.
